question: Which mode of political organisation unites separate states or other polities within an overarching political system in a way that allows each to maintain its own integrity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Federalism **__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• An essential feature of the **Federal System** is the **Division of powers.**
 
• **Federalism**, mode of political organization that unites separate states or other polities within an overarching political system in a way that allows each to maintain its own integrity.
 
• Unlike in a unitary state, sovereignty in federal political orders is **non-centralized,** often constitutionally, between at least two levels.
 
• Federalism is different from confederalism. In Confederalism the **general level of government is subordinate to the regional level.**
 
• It also differs from a **unitary state**, in which the **regional level of government is subordinate to the general level.**
 
• Some examples of the federation or federal state include the **United States, India, Brazil, Mexico, Russia, Germany, Canada, Switzerland, Argentina, and Australia.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian constitution borrowed the **concept of federalism** from the **constitution of Canada.**
 
• Integrity refers to the **wholeness** and **unity** of a nation.
 
• In a political context, it often refers to the **territorial integrity** of a country, meaning the preservation of its borders and sovereignty from external threats or interventions.
 
• Democracy is a system of government in which **the power is vested in the people**.
 
• It is a form of government where citizens have the right to participate in decision-making, either directly or through elected representatives.
 
• Sovereignty refers to the **supreme authority** of a state to govern itself, make laws, and conduct affairs without interference from external powers.
 
• It implies that a country has control over its territory, resources, and people.
